claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First of all, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know you'd like to claim for Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now, could you please tell me if you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. Now, could you tell me about your living situation with Alex? Does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you.

Just a couple more questions to confirm your eligibility:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One final question: Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any form of residential accommodation provided by the local council?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he was in care for a short while actually - just a couple of months earlier this year, but he's back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. I'm glad Alex is back home with you now.

Just to clarify, during the time Alex was in care, did he spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you, or was he away for the full period?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he was away for the full period - he was at the care home full-time during those couple of months.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex was in care for about 2 months (approximately 8 weeks), I have one more question:

During the time Alex was in care, did you make any contributions towards his upkeep (such as money for clothes, food, pocket money, or presents) that were at least equal to the Child Benefit amount?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I wasn't able to contribute financially during that time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being open about that.

Since Alex was in care for around 8 weeks and has now returned home to live with you full-time, and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him, I have enough information to assess your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me:

- You live in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- Alex now lives with you
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- Although he was in care for about 8 weeks earlier this year, he is now back home with you

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex is under 16 years old
- ✅ Alex lives with you
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

Regarding the time Alex spent in care earlier this year, since he was away for approximately 8 weeks and has now returned home to live with you, this does not affect your current eligibility. The rules state that Child Benefit may be affected if a child is in care for *more than* 8 weeks, and importantly, Alex is now back home with you.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask!
